title: Nvidia mean Street price target clears $300 on data-center GPU demand by Q4 2026
body: China Renaissance's June 5 Buy initiation at a $319 target reset the upper end of Nvidia's coverage roster, opening a wide gap above where US desks anchored the week prior (Needham at $270 on June 2). That spread is the tell: the bullish initiation rests on a soft-landing read of AI-accelerator demand, and the gap closes one of two ways. The prediction is that the mean published 12-month price target across covering sell-side analysts crosses $300 by the close of Q4 2026, dragged up rather than down. The mechanism is concrete and falsifiable on the hardware side: a data-center segment revenue print at or above a roughly $130B annualized run-rate (about $32B-plus in a single quarter) on the next two earnings reports is the condition under which laggard desks revise upward to track the China Renaissance high; a single sub-consensus data-center quarter, or a sharp gross-margin step-down signaling pricing pressure as inference fragments toward custom silicon and Groq-style LPUs, breaks the thesis and the mean stalls below $300. The cross-cutting claim is that the technical reality (data-center GPU revenue holding its run-rate as Nvidia widens into AI PCs and licensed accelerator lines) is what forces sell-side consensus to converge toward, not away from, the freshly-set Street high.

reasoning.because: China Renaissance opened Nvidia at Buy/$319 on Jun 5, well above Needham's $270 set Jun 2
reasoning.given: Data-center GPU revenue run-rate, not export or demand fear, is what laggard desks now mark to
reasoning.so_that: Slower-moving sell-side desks revise their 12-month targets up to track the Street high, lifting the mean past $300
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026 close; mean analyst PT > $300 after two data-center prints
reasoning.plain_language: One bank set a high $319 price tag on Nvidia; if chip sales stay strong, others raise their targets to match.

summary: China Renaissance's Jun 5 Buy initiation at $319 sits far above Needham's $270, a new high on Nvidia's roster. The prediction: the mean analyst 12-month price target clears $300 by Q4 2026, pulled up not down, conditioned on data-center GPU revenue holding a ~$130B run-rate over the next two prints.
